reading.body:
Alaska's AI-related legislative activity is narrow and early: of ten bills in this dataset, only a handful directly address AI, and their focus is on harms rather than governance infrastructure.

SB2 and SB33, both dated January 2025, cover deepfakes, synthetic media, cybersecurity, and election integrity. HB47 addresses AI-generated child sexual abuse material alongside social media. SB64 concerns elections and travels with a procedural resolution, HCR12, to suspend uniform rules. HCR3, a concurrent resolution from February 2025, establishes an AI legislative task force, which signals that Alaska's legislature treats itself as still in the study phase rather than the rulemaking phase. The remaining bills, covering nursing staffing, definitions of personhood, sustainability, and the operating budget, have no apparent AI-specific content, though the budget bill could theoretically touch AI procurement without the title indicating it.

None of these bills address compute infrastructure, data center siting, power consumption, or grid capacity. That absence is itself information: Alaska's legislature, as captured here through August 2026, has not engaged with the physical prerequisites of AI deployment. The dataset covers intent and status only through bill titles and dates, not outcomes, so it cannot say whether any of these measures passed, failed, or were amended.
